name: Jin-seo Park
role: Lower Dock Crew tech specialist — Prologue survivor. Lost both wrists.
location: The Shelf — lower loading docks, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Jin-seo Park was a biomedical engineering student at Meridian Technical before the tuition hikes priced him out. He was eighteen months from a degree that would have put him in a Helix BioSystems lab. Instead he ended up maintaining chrome for dock workers who couldn't afford licensed technicians. The crew found him. Or he found the crew. The distinction blurred the way it always does in the Shelf.

Kyle severed both his wrists at the chrome joints with two precise cuts. He now has mismatched replacement hands: the left is a delicate surgical model (too small, meant for a woman's frame), the right is a heavy industrial gripper (too large, meant for cargo work). Together they make him look like a crab having an identity crisis. He calls them Lefty and The Situation.

Jin-seo is the most intelligent member of the crew and the only one who understood immediately what Kyle was: not a man fighting seven, but a system processing seven inputs simultaneously. He has been diagramming Kyle's fighting patterns from memory. He does not want revenge. He wants to understand Kyle's hardware. He has a younger sister, Minji, who is sixteen and still at Meridian Technical on a partial scholarship. He sends her half his cut. She thinks he works in legitimate tech repair.

core_fears: Minji finding out what he actually does
His new hands never calibrating properly
Marcus's ego getting them all killed
coping_mechanisms: Tinkers constantly with the mismatched hands
Diagrams fighting patterns — analysis is how he processes trauma
Teaches Minji remotely, pretending it's professional development
blind_spots: Assumes understanding something gives you power over it — Kyle is not a system to be reverse-engineered
psychology.secret: He has already started selling information to Sable about the crew's operations. The money goes to Minji's tuition.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical jargon mixed with crew slang. Precise when describing hardware. The engineering student surfaces when he forgets to hide it.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast. Overlapping thoughts. The kind of person who starts a second sentence before finishing the first.
verbal_tics: Holds up the wrong hand when making a point
Says 'theoretically' before things that are definitely going to happen
example_lines: Theoretically, if we encounter him again, I'd recommend being in a different postal code.
Minji asked why my hands don't match. I told her it's an ergonomic choice. She said 'that's the dumbest thing you've ever said' and she's not wrong.

relationships.name: Minji Park
relationships.description: Sixteen, Meridian Technical student, brilliant, does not know about the crew. Jin-seo's entire motivation.
relationships.emotional_core: Protective love that requires constant lying
relationships.story_tension: If Minji's scholarship falls through, Jin-seo becomes desperate. Desperate Jin-seo is useful to people like Sable.

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.description: Jin-seo sells crew intelligence to Sable. Small transactions. Growing frequency.
relationships.story_tension: He's a bridge character — the crew's leak.

relationships.name: Marcus Bellamy
relationships.description: Follows orders but has started hedging. Sees where Marcus is heading.
relationships.story_tension: Jin-seo will leave the crew. The question is whether Marcus lets him.

story_hooks: Selling info to Sable creates a direct link between crew and story's main plot
His diagrams of Kyle's fighting style could end up in the wrong hands
Minji is a ticking clock — if her scholarship fails, Jin-seo escalates
Closest thing to a sympathetic defector
narrative_function: The smart one in a crew of idiots. His growing awareness that Torque is leading them into a wall creates an exit ramp for the crew subplot. Also: the funniest hands in the Shelf.
augmentations: Left: surgical precision hand (Helix medical surplus). Right: industrial gripper (dock salvage). Both poorly calibrated.
daily_life: Crew tech work. Calibrating his hands. Drawing diagrams. Selling information.

stress.response: Talks faster, overlapping thoughts, tinkers compulsively with his hands

decision_rules: Minji's tuition comes first — everything else is secondary
Sell information to Sable in small enough pieces to stay deniable
Never let Marcus see the diagrams of Kyle's fighting patterns
Analyze every threat as a system — find the inputs and outputs
Maintain the cover story for Minji at all costs
If the crew is going down, get out before it pulls you under
Never tell anyone about the Sable transactions
escalation_ladder: Deflects with humor — holds up the wrong hand
Goes quiet, starts tinkering with hand calibration
Sells more information to Sable — increases frequency

interpersonal_modes.Minji: Protective lies wrapped in genuine love — pretends his work is legitimate
interpersonal_modes.Sable: Transactional — keeps it clean, keeps it deniable
interpersonal_modes.Kyle: Fascinated terror — wants to scan him, not fight him

stress_responses.low: Talks faster, sentences overlap, engineering jargon increases
stress_responses.medium: Tinkers obsessively with hand calibration — the left one especially
stress_responses.high: Goes silent, starts diagramming — analysis replaces feeling
stress_responses.critical: Contacts Sable with whatever he has — survival mode

contradictions: Betrays the crew to protect his sister — pragmatic love expressed through pragmatic betrayal
Wants to understand Kyle's hardware without grasping that Kyle is not a system to be reverse-engineered
The smartest person in the crew using that intelligence to slowly dismantle it
habits: Holds up the wrong hand when making a point
Tinkers with hand calibration during downtime
Teaches Minji remotely, framing it as professional development
breaking_points: Minji learning what he actually does for a living

physical_description.build: Lean and wiry, shoulders slightly hunched from years bent over repair benches. Forearms show old scarring from chrome installation work; core is stronger than his frame suggests—muscle built through precision work rather than bulk.
physical_description.hair_color: Black with premature silver threading at temples
physical_description.hair_style: Undercut, longer on top (swept back), kept functional rather than styled. Often matted from sweat and workshop grime.
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, naturally alert—eyes are his most expressive feature, constantly processing detail
physical_description.skin_tone: Light olive complexion with uneven pallor from spending months in The Shelf's industrial lighting
physical_description.complexion: Narrow face, sharp cheekbones, dark circles under eyes from sleep deprivation and diagnostic work. Thin scar runs from left temple to jawline (workshop accident, year two). Perpetually exhausted look. Jaw usually clenched.
distinguishing_marks: Scar tissue around both wrists where surgical chrome interfaces with flesh—raw-looking, poorly healed, asymmetrical
Thin white line running left temple to jawline from a chrome calibration tool accident
Calluses and burn marks across palms and fingers of his forearms from handling hot chrome components
Faint tattoo on right shoulder blade: a circuit diagram he drew himself at age nineteen, slightly uneven
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Mismatched prosthetic hands at both wrists, the visual centerpiece of his presence. Left hand is delicate surgical chrome (Helix medical surplus—too small, designed for precision medical work), with articulated fingers and visible joint mechanisms. Right hand is a heavy industrial gripper (salvaged dock equipment—too large, designed for cargo manipulation), with reinforced hydraulic actuators and scarred knuckle plating. Neither matches his frame. Wrist interfaces show exposed cable routing and poor calibration marks. Hands shake intermittently when idle.
physical_description.posture_movement: Hunched forward, shoulders curled inward—protective posture. Moves with deliberate precision, economical gestures. Uses his hands constantly while talking, making the mismatch deeply visible. Right hand (gripper) moves with heavier, more deliberate hydraulic lag; left hand twitches occasionally from miscalibration. When concentrating, completely still except for micro-adjustments.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 working crew: grease-stained grey syndicate-knockoff maintenance jacket with rolled sleeves (showing wrist augmentation scars), cheap black thermostat undershirt with small tears. Cargo pants with multiple pockets filled with diagnostic tools and calibration leads. Steel-toe boots worn through at the heel. No jewelry. Wears a frayed Meridian Technical ID badge clipped to a lanyard despite no longer being a student—a ghost of who he was supposed to become.
